data.narrative:
Seneca operates in the Drones & Autonomous sector at Series A stage, having raised $60M to date. The sector comprises eight private peers including Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro, with no public comparables available for direct benchmarking.

Peer-Median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparable data within the Drones & Autonomous universe—fewer than three datapoints met the narrow filtering criteria necessary for reliable median derivation. Accordingly, Stage-Progression analysis anchored the valuation framework, using total capital raised ($60M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression. This method yielded an implied valuation of $120M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $102M to $138M, with a median point of $120M. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression midpoint to account for execution risk and fundraising environment volatility. Primary uncertainties stem from the absence of tight peer comparables and reliance on a single methodological input. Prospective investors should weight this valuation against company-specific traction metrics, competitive positioning within the five-peer peer set, and pathway to next funding stage. Additional comparable data from recent Series A and Series B closings in autonomous systems would meaningfully narrow this range.
